ticker: India Supreme Court drops two-child penalty
US slaps sanctions on Iranian oil network

articles.headline: US Democrats Secure Sweeping Congressional Midterm Victories
articles.brief: US Democrats achieved a major electoral victory in the midterm elections, capturing control of both chambers of Congress. The political shift introduces new legislative guardrails against the administration's current foreign and domestic agenda, sending ripples through global financial markets and triggering significant policy debates.

articles.headline: Global Markets Rally Following US Midterm Election Results
articles.brief: Global stock markets surged, with Indian benchmarks hitting three-month highs as oil prices slid following the Democratic sweep in the US. Investors welcomed the political shift and potential easing of geopolitical tensions, fueling a massive rally across major tech and equity sectors.

articles.headline: US Imposes Sanctions on Indian and Turkish Entities Over Iran
articles.brief: The United States has levied fresh sanctions against Indian and Turkish individuals and companies accused of facilitating the transportation of Iranian oil through fake vessel registrations and supporting Iranian aviation. The move marks an escalation in Washington's crackdown on Tehran's petroleum trade network.

articles.headline: India's IndiGo Discusses Acquisition of 100 Jets with Embraer
articles.brief: India's largest airline, IndiGo, is reportedly in advanced discussions with Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer to purchase up to 100 regional jets. This prospective mega-order highlights the carrier's aggressive strategy to expand its domestic and regional footprint amid booming aviation demand across South Asia.

articles.headline: Qualcomm Partners with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile 5G Network
articles.brief: Chipmaker Qualcomm has signed a definitive infrastructure agreement with SpaceX to integrate 5G capabilities with the Starlink Mobile network. The strategic partnership aims to bridge global connectivity gaps by delivering direct-to-cell satellite broadband services to standard smartphones worldwide.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules India's Two-Child Population Penalties Outdated
articles.brief: India's Supreme Court declared that two-child statutory penalties for local governance roles are outdated, noting that falling fertility rates and demographic shifts have neutralized historical overpopulation fears. The bench emphasized that the rolling impact of decelerating population growth presents long-term socio-economic challenges.

articles.headline: Delhi Grapples with Severe Air Pollution Crisis as AQI Hits 482
articles.brief: Delhi's air quality deteriorated to severe categories, with multiple monitoring stations recording an Air Quality Index peaking at 482. Local authorities have implemented strict vehicular and industrial restrictions utilizing AI-enabled control centers, while healthcare facilities report an alarming surge in patients suffering from acute respiratory distress.

articles.headline: India Draws $400 Billion in Preliminary Renewable Energy Pledges
articles.brief: The Indian government has secured approximately $400 billion in preliminary investment commitments at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit. Officials will review the proposals to advance grid-scale storage infrastructure and accelerate national targets for expanding non-fossil power generation capacity.

articles.headline: Pentagon CTO Acknowledges Ukraine's Advanced Drone Innovations
articles.brief: Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael admitted that Ukrainian forces developed crucial drone and combat technologies independently because standard US military stockpiles lacked them. The conflict has exposed gaps in Western defense manufacturing and prompted a strategic reassessment of modern warfare capabilities.

articles.headline: NASA's Swift Satellite Telescope Ends Mission in Fiery Reentry
articles.brief: NASA's 22-year-old Swift satellite telescope has completed its operational lifespan, burning up during an uncontrolled atmospheric reentry over the Earth. Launched in 2004, the observatory revolutionized astrophysics by detecting and tracking gamma-ray bursts across deep space.

articles.headline: India Accuses Beverage Giants of Misleading Energy Drink Labeling
articles.brief: Indian consumer protection regulators have stated that PepsiCo and Monster Beverage marketed certain products under 'energy drink' labels to mislead buyers. Authorities argue the branding practices obscure ingredient compositions, prompting closer scrutiny of marketing compliance within the domestic beverage sector.

articles.headline: Indian Tyre Manufacturers Face Margin Pressures Amid High Rubber Costs
articles.brief: Major Indian tyre producers, including JK Tyre and CEAT, reported sharp declines in quarterly profits and EBITDA due to escalating natural rubber prices. Companies are weighing further retail price hikes to offset input cost pressures that continue to squeeze automotive sector earnings.

articles.headline: Virat Kohli Celebrates 38th Birthday Amid Continued Cricket Legacy
articles.brief: Veteran Indian batsman Virat Kohli celebrated his 38th birthday, marking a storied career defined by numerous international batting records and a 2011 World Cup title. Observers continue to evaluate his fitness and form as he eyes future milestones, including the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup.

articles.headline: Two Oil Tankers and Tugboat Catch Fire in Strait of Hormuz
articles.brief: Two oil tankers and an accompanying tugboat caught fire in the strategic Strait of Hormuz following an unspecified maritime incident. Emergency marine units responded to the disaster as regional security forces monitor potential disruptions to vital international petroleum transit routes.

articles.headline: India Prioritizes Food Security Over Ethanol Goals Amid El Niño
articles.brief: The Indian government has recalibrated its domestic biofuel roadmap, prioritizing food grain availability over ethanol blending ambitions. Persistent weather anomalies and agricultural strain caused by El Niño conditions compelled policymakers to safeguard domestic food supplies against inflationary pressures.
